Even though the witness who signed the document first is disqualified, etc. Shach, seif katan 23, argues extensively for the dissenting authorities. He concludes that if the disqualified witness signed first, the document can be valid, but if he signed in the middle or at the end it is invalid. I have already stated many times that where the early authorities dispute, I do not consider myself one who can simply decide that one tradition is proper and the other improper. All the more so here, where even the great masters themselves revised their positions. Rabbenu Tam famously retracted because of the force of the difficulties raised against him. I therefore will not attempt to declare one view superior on authority alone. However, Shach claims a decisive proof from the Yerushalmi and, in order to make that proof work, he emends, adds, deletes, and reverses several parts of the text. In my view there is no need for such extensive emendation. Only one word appears to be an obvious scribal carryover, and once removed, the Yerushalmi reads smoothly and actually supports Rambam. The Yerushalmi in the first chapter of Gittin says: The Mishnah teaches that any get bearing the signature of a Samaritan witness is invalid, except certain gittin of women. The Yerushalmi asks: then even one Samaritan witness should make it invalid. R. Elazar answers: establish it where a Jewish witness signed last. R. Yochanan says this follows the view that witnesses may sign in each other's absence. According to the view that witnesses sign only in each other's presence, even if the Samaritan signed last the document is valid. The Yerushalmi then says: A document signed by four witnesses, where the first two are found to be relatives or disqualified, is valid and the testimony is established through the others. R. Elazar in the name of R. Yochanan says this follows the view that witnesses sign only in each other's presence. According to the view that witnesses may sign even in one another's absence, even if the disqualified one signed last, it is valid. That is the text before us. Shach objects because the Bavli appears to say the reverse regarding the Samaritan witness. He therefore rewrites the Yerushalmi extensively, changing whole clauses from valid to invalid and reversing the order of the positions. But even after his emendation, the final phrase about a Samaritan signing last does not fit the second discussion, which concerns ordinary relatives and disqualified witnesses, not Samaritans. The simpler explanation is that the final word "Israel" in one clause is a scribal remnant carried over from the earlier discussion of Samaritan and Jewish witnesses. Delete that one stray word, and the text makes sense without changing its structure. There is historical support. Razah in Gittin cites a version close to Shach's reconstructed reading, and Ramban in Milchamot apparently also had a different text. But Rambam's ruling in Hilchot Avadim strongly indicates he had our present Yerushalmi reading. Rambam rules that a get with one Samaritan witness can be valid without limiting the case to the Samaritan signing first and the Jewish witness signing last. Lechem Mishneh asks why Rambam omitted the Bavli's limitation. If the Samaritan must be a known chaver, moreover, then why should the rule be unique to gittin? The answer is that Rambam holds the initial Bavli establishment, requiring the Jewish witness to sign last, was rejected after the Gemara answers that get witnesses sign only in each other's presence. Once they sign together, the Jewish witness knows who will sign with him. A valid Jewish witness will not join with a Samaritan known to be untrustworthy. Therefore, so long as the Samaritan is presumed to be a chaver, the order of signatures no longer matters. Razah himself says that gittin were treated like the practice of the punctilious people of Jerusalem, who would not sign unless they knew who was signing with them. This is exactly Rambam's reasoning. The Yerushalmi states it expressly: according to the view that witnesses must sign together, even if the Samaritan signed last the get can be valid. That is the ruling Rambam adopts. Mechaber in the laws of slaves follows Rambam and likewise does not make validity depend on signature order. This strongly supports the accuracy of our Yerushalmi text. Now apply the same reasoning to the second half concerning four witnesses. The Yerushalmi says: If a document bears four witnesses and the first two are relatives or otherwise disqualified, it can still be valid through the remaining witnesses. The implication is that if the disqualified witnesses signed last, the matter may differ. Why? Not because a disqualified person's mere intent to testify automatically invalidates valid witnesses. The valid witnesses become disqualified only if they actually joined as a single witnessing unit with the invalid ones. This is the principle of Rif at the end of siman 36. If the valid witnesses signed first and the disqualified witnesses later added their names without the valid witnesses' knowledge, the original valid testimony should not be destroyed. That is almost self-evident. Two valid witnesses who already signed a proper document cannot be invalidated merely because some relatives later write their names beneath them without permission. But if witnesses are required to sign only in each other's presence, then when the disqualified witnesses sign last the valid witnesses necessarily know they are joining the same signing session. Since the disqualified witnesses sign last, their signatures are plainly intended as testimony rather than as mere filler. The valid witnesses knowingly join with them, and the entire witnessing unit becomes invalid. By contrast, if the law permits witnesses to sign in each other's absence, even a disqualified witness signing last does not prove the valid witnesses knew of him or joined with him. They may have completed their testimony earlier and never known the invalid person later added his signature. Therefore the valid witnesses remain valid. This is exactly the Yerushalmi's closing statement once the stray word is removed: according to the view that witnesses may sign separately, even if the disqualified witness signed last, the document is valid. Thus the Yerushalmi reads perfectly as written. And this is our halachah. Except for gittin, ordinary document witnesses may sign even outside one another's presence. Chazal did not decree ordinary documents because of gittin in this respect. Therefore, even if a disqualified witness signs at the end, we can say the valid witnesses never knew of him and never joined with him. The document remains valid through the valid signatures. Consider the simple case. Two competent witnesses sign a document completely and deliver it. Later, without their knowledge, a relative of one party adds his signature at the bottom. Can that later act retroactively destroy their valid testimony? That is unreasonable. The whole law of "one relative or disqualified witness invalidates the group" depends on actual joining into one witnessing unit, not on the physical coexistence of names on one page. The Yerushalmi therefore supports Rambam's broader approach. Shach lists many authorities who invalidate where the disqualified witness signs later. Even so, where the early authorities divide, the possessor can certainly say kim li like the minority. And this minority is weighty: Rambam, Ramban, Rav Hai Gaon, and Rivash. According to the reading explained here, the Yerushalmi itself also supports them. Therefore one certainly cannot remove property from the possessor against this view. There is also a parallel from the Samaritan-witness case. There, the entire significance of signing in one another's presence is that the valid Jewish witness knows whom he is joining. If he signs first and the Samaritan later signs without his knowledge, there is no joining. If he signs while aware the Samaritan will sign, the shared act creates the problem unless the Samaritan is one whom the Jewish witness could legitimately join. The same principle governs relatives and disqualified witnesses. The decisive question is not merely order. It is whether the valid witnesses knowingly joined the invalid witness in one act of testimony. Signature order is only evidence of that joining. Where signing can occur separately, later order proves nothing. Accordingly, the Yerushalmi's distinction is conceptually precise. One should therefore not rewrite its text to fit a preconceived rule. Its plain structure gives a coherent legal theory and aligns with Rambam and Mechaber. Thus, despite Shach's attempt to establish the opposite as definitive, the possessor has ample basis to rely on the validating authorities even where the disqualified witness signed last.
Unless the last two, etc. The wording implies that if disqualified witnesses signed in the middle, the document is still valid. Shach, however, cites the majority of authorities as holding that middle signatures of disqualified witnesses also invalidate the document. Beit Yosef cites Tosafot in the second chapter of Gittin as invalidating even where the disqualified witnesses signed in the middle. He was troubled that Rosh seemed to disagree and validate such a case. In Even HaEzer he treats them as disputing; in Choshen Mishpat he tries to reconcile them. Maharit already objected to that reconciliation, and Get Pashut discusses the difficulty at length. Rama in Even HaEzer also requires explanation. Tur first says that where the husband says, "All of you sign," two are treated as witnesses and the rest as satisfying a condition, so if those additional signers are disqualified the get can still be valid. Tur later says that if two disqualified witnesses sign first, the get is invalid. Darkei Moshe infers that the earlier validation referred only to disqualified witnesses signing later, and asks that if signing first invalidates, all the more so should signing later invalidate. He answers that Tur follows Rabbenu Tam's first position, before Rabbenu Tam retracted. This is difficult because here in Choshen Mishpat Tur explicitly follows Rabbenu Tam after his retraction and says that Rosh agreed with him. Maharsha likewise asks against Tosafot in Bava Batra 163b. Tosafot, following Rabbenu Tam, say that a disqualified witness signing first can sometimes be valid but signing last is invalid. Maharsha asks from Gittin, where the implication appears to be that only signing first invalidates, and answers that signing in the middle can be valid according to Rosh. Yet Tosafot in Gittin 18b explicitly say after Rabbenu Tam's retraction that even middle signatures can invalidate. The proper resolution is to distinguish the reasons for invalidity. Where disqualified witnesses sign after the first two valid witnesses, there are two possible concerns. First, their signatures may have been intended as actual testimony. Once the valid witnesses and invalid witnesses join in one testimonial act, the group is impaired. Second, people normally authenticate a document from its last witnesses. If disqualified witnesses appear at the end, a court may mistakenly authenticate the document through them. The second concern applies specifically when the invalid witnesses are last. It does not apply when they are in the middle because the court can authenticate from the final valid witnesses. The first concern, joining as testimony, operates differently in gittin. Ran explains that in a get the decisive intention is the husband's. We presume the husband does not deliberately designate disqualified persons as witnesses. Therefore a disqualified signer in the middle need not be understood as joining the witnessing unit. In ordinary monetary documents, by contrast, even if the parties did not intend the invalid signer as a witness, the signer himself may have intended to join the testimony. That is enough to create the problem discussed by Ran at length. Accordingly, in a get the primary concern can be authentication from the final signers. There the problem is specifically where the invalid witnesses are last, while middle invalid witnesses can be tolerated. This explains Rosh's answer in Gittin and Maharsha's reconciliation. But in ordinary monetary documents, the concern of testimonial joining remains even for middle signatures. Tosafot in Gittin, when discussing the Bava Batra document case, therefore say that even middle disqualified witnesses can invalidate. Thus Tosafot and Rosh need not disagree at all. They are speaking about different document categories. Tur in Even HaEzer can likewise be understood without forcing him into Rabbenu Tam's abandoned position. His statement that later disqualified signers can be valid refers to the get setting, where middle signers do not necessarily create the same testimonial joining problem. His Choshen Mishpat ruling can remain stricter for ordinary documents. This is also the better practical law. At first I was troubled because Tur here says "the last two" invalidate, which sounds as though only the final signers matter. His abridged rulings likewise speak of disqualified witnesses signing "at the end." But Beit Yosef himself notes that Tur's wording does not clearly decide the middle case. The word "last" can be used loosely to mean any signers after the original first witnesses, not necessarily the final two at the bottom. Indeed, in Rosh's abridged rulings to Gittin, he writes that if a relative signed "after the first two" the get is valid. That phrase clearly includes a middle signer, because the actual last signer may still be valid. This supports reading Tur's "last" language in Choshen Mishpat as excluding only the first position rather than defining the exact final position. Accordingly, the correct rule is as Shach states: in ordinary documents, a disqualified witness who signs in the middle also invalidates when his signature is part of the testimonial unit. There is a possible proof from Tosafot in Bava Batra concerning a document whose text is on ordinary parchment and whose witnesses are on erased parchment. Tosafot ask why the witnesses need to write, "We witnesses are signed on erased parchment." Why not simply leave blank space? In a document with only two witnesses, one can understand the concern. But if there are three witnesses, leaving a gap between the first and the last two creates a possibility that the holder will later fill the blank with relatives or disqualified persons. If middle disqualified signatures were always harmless, that would not be a serious problem. This supports the view that in ordinary documents they can invalidate. One can answer that the Tosafot case may have different anti-forgery features, as I explained in my novellae. In particular, where the document text is on ordinary parchment and witnesses are on erased parchment, any opening for later manipulation can make the original paper improper because the holder could later cut, erase, and reconstruct it in a different configuration. But the broader point remains. The distinction between gittin and monetary documents gives the cleanest reconciliation of the early authorities. There is another way to understand Tosafot's concern. Suppose two borrowers borrow jointly from one lender and sign a handwritten statement on ordinary parchment while their signatures are on erased parchment. Even if that document lacks the full force of a formal witness-signed note, the borrowers may trust the lender not to alter it. He could later erase and rewrite the document so that the borrowers' own signatures appear as witnesses to a different person's debt. The danger exists because the signers themselves may be valid witnesses relative to that third person. Tosafot's statement that people do not hand over an instrument capable of such fraud can therefore refer not only to professional witnesses but to ordinary Jews generally. One does not intentionally place a stumbling block before another person. This explains why the anti-forgery rules remain strict even where the exact witness-order question is disputed. In practical halachah, however, the distinction stated above is sufficient: for gittin, middle disqualified signatures can be tolerated under the relevant theory because the husband's intent controls and the main concern is authentication from the end; for ordinary civil documents, middle disqualified witnesses can invalidate because their own intent to testify creates a problematic testimonial joining. This is the conclusion supported by Shach and by the stronger reading of Tosafot.
The last ones, etc. The principal reason is that documents are ordinarily authenticated from the final witnesses. If the last witnesses are disqualified, the court may end up authenticating the document through disqualified testimony. Shach discusses this at length. One difficulty remains. Rosh asks: if relatives can sign, should we not fear that the document will later be authenticated through them, just as the Gemara fears in the case of a folded get? He answers that ordinary documents are authenticated only from the final witnesses, and those final witnesses must always be valid. But then consider the Gemara's concern where witnesses left a one-line gap between the text and the signatures. The holder may cut away the original text, write a new one-line document together with one witness, and say that the additional signatures were merely added to increase the number of witnesses. The Gemara answers that in such a case the court authenticates from the upper witnesses. Why does that solve the problem? The forger could write the one-line document and sign disqualified witnesses in the added area. Then when the court authenticates from the upper witnesses, it would authenticate through disqualified witnesses, which is exactly Rosh's original concern. If we answer that the court always investigates whether the witnesses are valid, then Rosh's entire concern disappears, as Ramban already notes. Even if relatives are not suspected of deliberately signing a fabricated document, the question remains from witnesses disqualified because they are presumed unreliable. The answer is that the two cases involve different procedural postures. When the debtor claims the document is forged, beit din investigates the witness identities carefully. A person ordinarily does not brazenly call a genuine document forged, and the Torah itself does not strictly require formal document authentication absent a challenge. Once he does challenge it, the court scrutinizes the signers and will discover whether they are disqualified. Therefore the forged one-line document does not create the danger. Rosh's concern arises in a different case. Suppose the debtor admits that the document was genuinely written but claims some other defense. Under the rule that one who admits the writing may still require authentication in order to eliminate his migo, the creditor seeks technical authentication. In that setting, the court already knows the underlying document is real. It may perform only the limited authentication needed to remove the debtor's migo and may not investigate every signer's personal qualification with the same intensity. If the final signatures are relatives or disqualified persons, the court can mistakenly authenticate through them and deprive the debtor of his migo. That is the exact concern of Rosh. Thus there is no contradiction. When forgery is alleged, the court investigates the signers and does not rely blindly on invalid witnesses. When authenticity is admitted and the only need for authentication is procedural, the court may rely on the final signatures unless the document form prevents that. For this reason the final witnesses must be valid. The distinction also explains Tosafot's wording. Their concern is not that a competent court will knowingly accept disqualified witnesses. It is that ordinary document practice directs authentication to the final signers, and people may thereby come to rely upon a facially regular but legally improper configuration. The rule is therefore structural. Accordingly, the law that the final witnesses must be valid stands even though a court faced with a direct forgery claim would investigate more deeply.

urim_vetumim_urim.he: ואם הרחיקו וכו' דיכול לזייף ולחתוך כל שטר שלמעלה ולכתוב שטר חדש במה שירצה בב' שיטות הללו ועדים חתומים עליו עיין תומים מ"ש דלמה נקט חשש זה בסמ"ע ובב"י:
urim_vetumim_urim.en: If they left a space, etc. The concern is that one can cut away everything above and write a new document in those two blank lines, leaving the original witnesses' signatures beneath it. See Tumim for why Beit Yosef and Sema frame the concern in this manner.

mechaber.he: אם נפסל ע"י חתימת הפסולים אם הכשרים זוכרים העדות על ידי ראיית השטר יכולים להעיד וב"ד יכתבו עדותן כמו שכתוב בשטר וחשוב כמו שטר הראשון:
mechaber.en: If we are sculpted by the stamp signature if the talent remembers the evidence by seeing the bill can testify and in the D. they will write their testimony as written in the banner and as important as the first note:

baer_hetev.he:
וב"ד. נ"ל דוקא ב"ד אבל הם עצמן לא שלא נעשו שלוחים לחתום את השטר אלא בצירוף הפסול וכבר עשו שליחותן. ש"ך. * וא"ל הא כתב המחבר בסי' מ"ט ס"ו והביאו הסמ"ע והש"ך בסי' מ"א דאם יתבטל השטר לגמרי לא אמרינן דעשו שליחותן שאני התם דנעשו שלוחים על שטר כשר אבל הכא נעשו שלוחים על שטר פסול שיחתמו בצירוף הפסול ולכך אמרינן דכבר עשו שליחותן וק"ל:
וחשוב. כתב הסמ"ע והא דבסי' ל"ו כתב הט"ו דאם העידו יחד נפסל גם עדות הכשרים שאני התם שהעידו על פה בב"ד יחד ושוב אין תיקון לחזור ולהעיד לבדן משא"כ כאן דלא הגידו בע"פ בב"ד יחד והש"ך תירץ דכאן מיירי שהפסולים לא היו עמהם בשעת ראי' ולא הוצרכו לבאר זה דפשיטא דכשהיו עמהם דבטל העדות לגמרי לכ"ע דה"ל ראיי' והגד' דעדים החתומים על השטר כמי שנחקר' כו' ומה"ט קי"ל בכל דוכתי דהחתומים על השטר א"י לחזור ולהעיד דכיון שהגיד כו' והגד' בשטר כהגד' בב"ד דמיא ולמ"ש בסי' ל"ו דבהצטרפות לראי' לחוד בטל העדות אפילו לא העידו אח"כ א"כ אם היו פסולים עמהם בשעת ראיית המעש' נתבטל העדות אפילו לא חתמו בשטר ואם לא היו עמהם וחתמו על השטר ג"כ פסול הוי דאע"ג דכתבתי שם דבהגד' בב"ד לחוד לא נצטרפו הגד' דבשטר גרע טפי כיון דחתומים יחד על שטר אחר וה"ל מזויף מתוכו עכ"ל וע"ש:
baer_hetev.en:
And beit din. It appears to me that specifically beit din may remedy it, but the witnesses themselves may not, because they were appointed as agents to sign the document only together with the disqualified witness, and they have already discharged their agency. Shach. One should not object from the Mechaber's ruling in siman 49, seif 6, cited by the Sema and Shach in siman 41, that if the document would otherwise become entirely void we do not say that the witnesses have already discharged their agency. There the witnesses were appointed to produce a valid document. Here, by contrast, they were appointed to produce a defective document by signing together with the disqualified witness. We therefore say that their agency has already been discharged.
And it is considered. The Sema writes that although in siman 36 the Tur and Shulchan Aruch rule that when valid and disqualified witnesses testify together the testimony of the valid witnesses is also invalidated, there the testimony was delivered orally together before beit din, after which there is no way to repair it by having the valid witnesses testify again alone. Here, however, they did not give oral testimony together before beit din. The Shach answers that here the case is where the disqualified witnesses were not present with the valid ones when they observed the event. The authorities did not need to state this explicitly, because if they were together at the time of observation, the testimony is plainly void according to all opinions, since both the observation and the testimony were joined. Witnesses signed on a document are regarded as though their testimony had been examined in beit din, and for this reason we rule everywhere that witnesses signed on a document cannot later retract and testify differently, since once a witness has testified he cannot testify again. Testimony in a document is like testimony before beit din. According to what I wrote in siman 36, that joining together merely for observation invalidates the testimony even if they did not subsequently testify together, if the disqualified witnesses were present with them when the event was observed, the testimony was already void even before they signed. If they were not present together then, but they all signed the document, it is likewise invalid. Although I wrote there that merely giving testimony before beit din does not necessarily constitute joinder, testimony in a document is worse in this respect because all the witnesses are signed together on one document, rendering it intrinsically defective.

beer_hagolah.he: ט) טור בשם תשובת אביו הרא"ש סוף כלל ס'
beer_hagolah.en: A column called his father's answer

beur_hagra.he:
אם נפסל. מכות ו' א' אי למיחזי כו' ועתוס' שם ד"ה אי ופי' ר' חיים כו' וה"נ לא נפסל העדות שראו קודם כתיבת השטר:
ע"י ראיית. כתובות כ"א:
וב"ד. ב"ב קע"א א':
beur_hagra.en:
If it was disqualified. Makkot 6a, "If they came to observe," etc.; see Tosafot there, s.v. "if," and the explanation of Rabbeinu Chaim. Here too, the testimony that they witnessed before the writing of the document is not disqualified.
Through seeing. Ketubot 21b.
And beit din. Bava Batra 171a.

chelkat_mechokek.he: רק אבי החתן שלח. נראה אם אבי החתן נתן הסבלונות לשליח במעמד החתן והחתן שתק או שאמר הוליך זה לכלה בשם החתן ודאי זיכה לו הסבלונות וכבר נתבאר לעיל סי' ל"ה סעיף ד' בא' שגילה דעתו לשדכן שחפץ באשה פלונית והלך השדכן וקדש' וכן נתבאר לעיל בסימן ל"ה סעיף ה' אם הרצה האב לפני הבן ושתק הבן אמרינן דשתק הבן מחמת כסופ' וקידושי האב הוו ספק קידושין א"כ פשוט באתרא דרוב' מקדשי והדר מסבלי דיש לחוש לקידושי האב ואפילו למיעוט אפשר יש לחוש לגי' ר"ח והריב"ש לא כתב רק דק"ל כרבינא (קדושין דף מ"ה ע"א בעובד' דבי תרי דשתו חמר' הועתק לעיל בדברי המחבר סימן ל"ה ס"ק י"ב) דלא חיישינן דלמ' שליח שויא או ארצוי קמיה אבל אם באמת ארצויי קמי' ודאי חוששין לסבלונו':
chelkat_mechokek.en: Only the groom's father sent them. If the groom's father gave the gifts to the messenger in the groom's presence and the groom remained silent, or said, "Take these to the bride in the groom's name," then the father certainly conferred the gifts upon his son for this purpose. Above in siman 35:4 it was explained that where a man revealed to the matchmaker that he desired a certain woman and the matchmaker then betrothed her for him, there is concern. Likewise, in siman 35:5, if the father proposed the matter before the son and the son remained silent, we say that he may have been silent from embarrassment and the father's kiddushin are at least doubtful. Therefore, in a place where most people betroth before gifts, there is plainly concern for kiddushin arranged by the father. Even according to a minority practice there may be concern under the readings of Rabbeinu Chananel. Rivash ruled only that we follow Ravina and do not invent an agency or prior consent without evidence. But where the father actually proposed the matter to the son, we certainly take the gifts seriously.

ketzot_hachoshen.he: זוכרין העדות. עש"ך שכתב ז"ל ולפי מה שהעליתי לעיל סימן ל"ו דבנצטרף בראי' לחוד פסול כל העדות אפילו לא העידו אח"כ אם כן אם היו הפסולים בשעת ראי' נתבטל העדות אפילו לא חתמו בשטר עיין שם ולי נראה בשטר הלואה אף על גב דראו הלואת המעות יחד כל שחתמו הכשרים אח"כ עפ"י ציווי הלוה ולא ציוה אל הפסולים לחתוספות והפסולי' ציוה אח"כ לחתום (אח"כ) בזה ודאי השטר כשר עפ"י הכשרים דאף על גב דראו כאחד הלואות המעות מכל מקום דל מהכא הלואת המעות הרי הוא נתחייב עפ"י השטר אף על פי שאינו חייב כמבואר בסימן מ' והרי הוא כאלו ראו הלואה יחד עם הפסולים ואם כן שמעו הכשרי' שהודה לפניהם שחייב בזה ודאי דל הלואה הרי נתחייב עפ"י הודאה אלא אם ציוה לחתום הכשרים עם הפסולים דכיון ששמעו יחד ציווי הלוה לחתום וציווי לחתום היא ראייתן ועיין פ' השולח (גיטין דף ל"ג) ובזה אף על גב דחתמו הכשרים לבד כבר נצטרפו בראי' עם הפסולים דציווי לחתום היא ראייתן וחתימתן הוא הגדתן ואם כן כיון דשמעו יחד ציווי לחתום כבר נצטרפו בראי' ואולי מזה מיירי הש"ך אבל היכא דלא ציוה כי אם אל הכשרים אף על גב דראו יחד הלואת המעות אמרינן סלק הלוא' ונתחייב ע"י השט' שחותמין בו הכשרים וכמ"ש וז"ב:
ketzot_hachoshen.en: They remember the testimony. The Shach writes that if disqualified persons were already present at the time of seeing the loan, all the testimony is void even if they never later testified, because joinder at the seeing stage itself can nullify the qualified witnesses. In my view this is not necessarily so for a loan document. Even if all saw the transfer of money together, if the borrower later instructed only the qualified witnesses to sign, the document can rest upon the new obligation created through his formal written undertaking. Disregard the original transfer of money. By instructing qualified witnesses to sign, he creates a valid written obligation even apart from the prior loan, as explained in siman 40. The qualified witnesses then witness his new admission or undertaking, not the earlier viewing shared with disqualified people. Only if he instructed both qualified and disqualified witnesses together to sign do they join at the relevant seeing stage, because his command to sign is itself the witnessing event and their signatures are the testimony. Perhaps this is the Shach's intended case. But where he instructed only the qualified witnesses, the earlier joint observation of the loan does not invalidate the later document.

meirat_einayim.he: אם הכשרי' זוכרי' העדות כו' וכ"כ הטור והמחבר לקמן בסי' נ"א ועי' לעיל סוף סי' ל"ו דכתב הטור והמחבר דעת הרא"ש דאם העידו יחד דנפסל גם עדות כשרי' שאני התם שהעידו על פה בב"ד יחד וכיון דראו מתחלה יחד וגם העידו בב"ד נפסלו בשעת הגדתן ושוב אין תיקון כאשר יחזרו ויעידו לבדן משא"כ כאן דלא הגידו יחד בע"פ בב"ד ועד"ר סי"ט שם כתבתי דדין זה נלמד ממ"ש הרא"ש בכלל ס' דין ג' בדין צוואה ושם כתבתי דממ"ש הרא"ש שם בסי' ד' ה' נראה כסותר למ"ש בסי' ג' ששם כתב דאפילו כשחותמים בשטר אין לכשרים לחזור ולהעיד אא"כ כשהפסולים לא היה עמהם בראיית ההלואה אלא שישבו אחר כך וחתמו יחד ומ"ה אמרינן דהשטר פסול והעדות כשר ולא כשהיו הפסולין עמהן וכיונו להעיד גם בשעת הלואה ונדחקתי וכתבתי דמ"ש בדין ה' לא כ"כ כ"א לדעת הרמב"ם דס"ל דבראיה לחוד מפסל העדות אבל הרא"ש ס"ל דתרתי בעינן ראיה והגדה וכמ"ש הטור בסי' ל"ו מ"ה כתב שם בדין ג' דיכולין הכשרי' החתומי' על השטר לחזור ולהעיד והוא דוחק וצ"ע:
meirat_einayim.en: If the valid witnesses remember the testimony. The Tur and Mechaber write similarly below in siman 51. Above, at the end of siman 36, they cite the Rosh that if valid and invalid witnesses testified orally together, the valid testimony is also disqualified. That case differs because they testified together orally in beit din. Since they originally saw the event together and then testified together, the disqualification attached at the time of their oral testimony and cannot later be cured by having the valid witnesses testify again alone. Here they did not give oral testimony together before beit din. In Derishah on siman 36 I explained that this ruling derives from the Rosh, rule 60, siman 3, concerning a will. Yet the Rosh in simanim 4 and 5 there appears to contradict it, implying that even where witnesses signed a document the valid ones cannot return and testify unless the disqualified witnesses were not present with them when the loan was witnessed but joined only later to sign. If the disqualified witnesses were present and intended to testify already at the time of the loan, the valid witnesses could not later testify alone. I suggested with difficulty that the latter statements were written according to Rambam, who holds that mere joint witnessing can invalidate the testimony, while the Rosh himself requires both joint witnessing and joint testimony. This remains difficult and requires study.

netivot_hamishpat_beurim.he: אם הכשרים זוכרין העדות. עיין ש"ך סעיף קטן ך"ה דדוקא ב"ד אבל הם עצמם לא שכבר עשו שליחותן שלא נעשו שלוחים לחתום השטר אלא בצירוף הפסול עכ"ל ותמוה לי דאם לא נעשו שלוחים לחתום רק בצירוף הפסול אם כן לא נעשו שלוחים לעשות שטר כשר כלל והאיך יכולין לפלוני מנה יכולין לכתוב שטר:
netivot_hamishpat_beurim.en: If the qualified witnesses remember the testimony. See Shach, seif katan 25, who writes that only beit din may act upon this, but the witnesses themselves may not, because they already completed their agency. They had been appointed to sign the document only together with the disqualified witness. This is difficult. If they were appointed to sign only together with the disqualified witness, then they were never appointed to create a valid document at all. How, then, can they write a new document stating that so and so owes a maneh?

netivot_hamishpat_hidushim.he: זוכרים העדות. ודוקא הב"ד אבל הם בעצמם לא דכבר עשו שליחתן) (וע"ב דדוקא בקנין אבל בלא קנין אפי' הב"ד אין כותבין שטר אחר ואם ראו המעשה ביחד א"י להגיד בפה שכבר נתבטל משעת ראיה) (וע"ב דמ"מ אם חזר ואמר להם הלוה כתבו וחתמו יכולין לכתוב שטר אחר:
netivot_hamishpat_hidushim.en: Remember the evidence. But they themselves did not do so much to send them, but they did not write a different note, and if they saw the act together, they would say in the mouth that we had already been cancelled for an hour of evidence

pitchei_teshuva.he: אם הכשרים זוכרים. עי' סמ"ע וש"ך מה שהקשו דתשו' הרא"ש סותרים זא"ז וע' בתשובת כנסת יחזקאל סי' פ"ח שתירץ בטוב ע"ש וע' דברי משפט מ"ש בזה:
pitchei_teshuva.en: If the qualified witnesses remember. See Sema and Shach, who ask that the responsa of the Rosh appear to contradict one another. See Responsa Knesset Yechezkel, siman 88, who resolves the contradiction well. See also Divrei Mishpat regarding this issue.

siftei_kohen.he:
[" אם הכשרים זוכרי' כו' זהו מתשובת הרא\"ש כלל ס' דין ג' וכתב בסמ\"ע ס\"ק ל\"ד דממ\"ש הרא\"ש בתשובה שם סי' ה' נראה כסותר למ\"ש בסי' ג' ששם כ' דאפי' כשחותמי' בשטר אין לכשרים לחזור ולהעיד אלא א\"כ שהפסולי' לא היו עמהם בראיית ההלואה אלא שישבו אח\"כ וחתמו יחד ומ\"ה אמרי' דהשטר פסול והעדות כשר ולא כשהיו הפסולי' עמהן וכוונו להעיד גם בשעת הלואה ואפשר דמ\"ש בדין ה' לא כ\"כ כ\"א לדעת הרמב\"ם דס\"ל דבראיה לחוד מפסל העדות אבל הרא\"ש ס\"ל דתרתי בעינן ראיה והגדה וכמ\"ש הטור בסי' ל\"ו מ\"ה כתב שם בדין ג' דיכולי' החתומי' על השטר לחזור ולהעיד ודוחק וצ\"ע עכ\"ל ולא נהירא אלא נראה דהרא\"ש בסי' ג' וכן המחבר כאן מיירי שהפסולי' לא היו עמהם בשעת ראיה ולא הוצרכו לבאר זה דפשיטא דכשהפסולי' היו עמהם דבטל העדות לכ\"ע דהא ה\"ל ראיה והגדה דעדי' החתומי' על השטר כמו שנחקרה עדותן בב\"ד דמי ומה\"ט קי\"ל בכל דוכתי עדי' החתומי' על השטר אין יכולים לחזור ולהעיד דכיון שהגיד שוב אינו חוזר ומגיד דהגדה בשטר כהגדה בב\"ד היא כן נ\"ל: ולפי מה שהעליתי לעיל סי' ל\"ו סק\"ח דבנצטרפו בראיה לחוד בטל העדו' אפילו לא העידו אח\"כ א\"כ אם היו הפסולי' עמהם בשעת ראית המעש' נתבטל העדות אפילו לא חתמו בשטר ואם לא היו הפסולי' עמהם בשעת ראיית המעשה וחתמו על השטר פסול דאע\"ג דהעליתי לעיל סי' ל\"ו ס\"ק ו' דבהגדה לחוד לפני ב\"ד לא נצטרפו ודלא כהרמ\"ה הגדה דבשטר גרע טפי כיון דחתומי' יחד על שטר א' וה\"ל מזויף מתוכו וגם כיון דאין העדי' חותמי' על השטר אלא מדעת המתחייב שאומר להם כתובו וחתומו א\"כ חתימתן על השטר הוי צירוף לענין מעשה השטר כיון שצרפן יחד לחתום על שטר א' אבל ראיית המעש' לא נתבטל דראיית המעש' וחתימת השטר שני ענינים מחולקי' הם כן נ\"ל ודלא כמהר\"מ אלשקר בתשובה סי' ט\"ז דף כ\"ד ע\"א שכ' דמדפסל הרמב\"ם שטר שחתומים עליו קרובים או פסולי' מוכח דס\"ל כהרמ\"ה דהא כתב אם יש עדות ברורה שישבו כולם לחתום כו' ולא קאמר אם יש עדות דבשע' שראו היו כולם ביחד דהא אפשר דהעדות קיתה בזמן א' והחתימה מאוחרת כו' והאריך שם בזה וליתא אלא כמ\"ש דהשתא לא עסקינן אלא שהשטר בטל אבל מענין המעש' לא מיירי והשטר בטל מ\"מ מטעמא שכתבתי והא ראיה שהרי הרא\"ש וטור לעיל סי' ל\"ו ושאר פוסקי' לא ס\"ל כהרמ\"ה ואפ\"ה פסלי בשטר אלא ודאי כמ\"ש (ומ\"ש הנ\"י פרק ז\"ב בשם בעל העיטור ומביאו ב\"י סי' נ\"א ס\"ה דאין משביעים ע\"פ האחד הכשר שבא להעיד בע\"פ וכן משמע בתשובת רשב\"א שהביא ב\"י לעיל ס\"ס ל\"ו מיירי שנצטרפו יחד בשעת ראיית המעש' ודוק):"]
[" ובית דין יכתבו עדותן כו'. נ\"ל דוקא קאמר בית דין אבל הם עצמם לא שכבר עשו שליחותן שלא נעשו שלוחי' לחתום את השטר אלא בצירוף הפסול ודוק:"]
siftei_kohen.en:
If the valid witnesses remember. This is from a responsum of the Rosh. The Sema sees a contradiction between two responsa, but there is none. The present ruling concerns a case in which the disqualified witnesses were not present when the loan was seen; they joined only later in signing. If they had also joined in seeing the event with intent to testify, the testimony would be void according to all views, since signatures upon a deed are equivalent to testimony received in beit din. As explained in siman 36, joining in the observation itself may invalidate the testimony even without later testimony. If the disqualified persons were absent from the event but later signed the deed, the document is invalid because all signed together upon one instrument and the instrument is internally defective. Nevertheless, the valid witnesses may testify orally to the underlying transaction, because witnessing the event and signing the defective deed are distinct matters. This is contrary to Maharam Alshakar, who infers from Rambam that the original observation itself was necessarily void.
"And the court shall write their testimony as well." We are told by a court, but they themselves have not already made their mission not to sign the bill, but rather with the consolation and precision

turei_zahav.he: (שם והגאונים לא חלקו וכו') קשה כיון דתלוי הטעם ברווחא שביק וכו' מנ"ל דפוסלין אפי' בחתמו פסולים לבסוף דהתם לא שייך הרווחה שביק וי"ל דרבינו הוכיח מדכתבו הגאונים הטעם בחתמו פסולים תחלה מכח רווחא שביק ולא מחמת שחתמו לשם מילוי אלא ודאי דלא מבעיא קאמר לא מבעיא בסוף פשיטא דכשר דאפשר דחתמו בלא דעת הראשונים הכשרים אלא אפי' חתמו תחלה ר"ל [י"ל] דנעשה שלא מדעת הכשרים דרווחא שביק וכו':
turei_zahav.en: (There: and the Geonim did not distinguish, etc.) It is difficult. Since the reason depends upon the principle that the valid witnesses left space, etc., how do we know that the Geonim disqualify even where the invalid witnesses signed at the end, where that reasoning does not apply? One may answer that our master inferred this from the Geonim's explanation of the case where invalid witnesses signed first. They explain it through the rule that the valid witnesses left space, rather than because the invalid witnesses merely signed as fillers. Necessarily, their formulation is one of "not only." Not only where the invalid witnesses signed at the end is the document clearly valid, because perhaps they signed without the knowledge of the earlier valid witnesses; even where they signed first, one may still say that this occurred without the knowledge of the valid witnesses, because the valid witnesses left space. This is the meaning.

urim_vetumim_urim.he: חתמו על טיוטא הן שטייט לגמרי והן ששרט רק שריטה ונקודות דניכר דלא היה כתוב בו ואין צריך לקיים מכל מקום יאמרו דהעידו על זה דלית ביה ריעותא ועיין תומים מה שכתבתי בזה בישוב הסמ"ע:
urim_vetumim_urim.en: They have signed a draft entirely, and only scratched by scratches and points of Danel was written in it and should not be held anywhere, Daodo will say that a bucket of hysteria will be heard and see the charges I have written in this statement:

mechaber.he: היו העדים מרוחקים מהכתב יתר על שני שטין והיה הריוח שבין הכתב והעדים מלא בעדים פסולים או קרובים ה"ז כשר שהרי אינו יכול להזדייף ואם נראה השטר בב"ד קודם שמילאוהו בקרובים או פסולים שוב אין לו תקנה אבל אם הוכשר ע"י מילוי קרובים קודם שבא לב"ד אפי' עשאו המלוה מדעתו שלא מדעת הלוה כשר וי"א דדוקא שמילאוהו מדעת הלוה אבל אם מילאוהו שלא מדעת הלוה פסול:
mechaber.en: If the witnesses' signatures are more than two lines below the text, but the space between the text and the signatures is filled with signatures of related or disqualified people, the document is valid because it cannot be falsified. If the document was seen by a beit din before that space was filled, it can no longer be repaired. If it was made valid by filling the space with related signatures before reaching beit din, it is valid even if the lender did so on his own initiative without the borrower's knowledge. Some say it is valid only if the space was filled with the borrower's consent; otherwise it is invalid.

baer_hetev.he: מדעתו. ז"ל הסמ"ע נרא' פשוט דס"ל דיכול המלו' למלאותו מדעתו בקרובים אפילו אחר היום שנחתם כ"ז שלא נרא' בב"ד וכן מוכח באשר"י כו' וא"כ קשה דלא ה"ל להמחבר לסתום בסט"ו שלא כדעת הרא"ש ולכך נרא' שהכל סעיף א' הוא וצריך להגיה וי"ו וצ"ל והא דמכשרינן כו' עכ"ל והש"ך כתב דלא נהירא אלא דס"ל דכ"ע מודו בזה דנהי דיכול לעשותו שלא מדעת הלו' היינו כיון שמסר השטר לידו כאלו הרשהו לעשות אבל מ"מ אין השטר נכשר אלא משעת המלוי וכ"כ הט"ז דהדין שבסט"ו הוא אליבא דכ"ע והכי נקטינן עכ"ל):
baer_hetev.en: On his own initiative. The Sema writes: It appears obvious that according to this view the creditor may, on his own initiative, fill the remaining signature spaces with relatives even after the date on which the document was signed, so long as the document has not yet appeared before beit din. This is also evident from the Rosh. If so, it is difficult that in seif 15 the Mechaber writes without qualification contrary to the Rosh. It therefore appears that the two paragraphs are really one seif, and a conjunction should be inserted so that it reads, “And that which we validate...” The Shach writes that this is unconvincing. Rather, all authorities agree to the distinction: although the creditor may fill the spaces without the borrower's express consent, because delivery of the document to him is equivalent to authorization to do so, the document does not become valid until the time the spaces are actually filled. The Taz likewise writes that the rule in seif 15 follows all opinions, and this is the ruling we adopt.

beer_hagolah.he:
י) מבריית' דלעיל וכחזקיה שם
כ) טור בשם הר"ר יונה בשם י"א ושכן הסכים אביו הרא"ש
(דאלמוהו רבנן תקנתייהו ואמרו כל שטר שנראה בב"ד שלא נעשה כתקון חכמים הרי הוא כחספא בעלמא סמ"ע)

A column in the name of Rabbi Yona in the name of G-d, and his father agreed
The Sages strengthened their enactment and said that any document appearing before beit din that was not prepared according to rabbinic requirements is like a mere shard of pottery. Sema.
There in the name of Rabbenu Yonah. The Maggid Mishneh likewise writes in his name at the end of Hilkhot Malveh.

beur_hagra.he: (ליקוט) ואם נראה כו' וי"א כו'. מדאמרי' הרחיק שני שטין פסול אמאי פסול יצוו הב"ד למלאות עדיין (ע"כ)
beur_hagra.en: (Anthology) And if it appears, etc.; and some say, etc. The Gemara says that if one left a space of two lines the document is invalid. Why should it be invalid? Beit din could still order that the space be filled. This supports the latter opinion.

chelkat_mechokek.he: לא חיישינן כולי האי. כלו' די לנו אם נחמיר בקול בקידושין גמורין או בודאי שליחות וסבלונות אבל לצרף שתי חששות ולחוש לקלא דסבלונות כולי האי לא חיישינן:
chelkat_mechokek.en: I don't enjoy the whole island. Allo is sufficient for us if we are ashamed of the fullness or certainly a mission and suffering, but to attach two fears and to the senses to the failure of all the sufferings of the island, which is not their life:

meirat_einayim.he:
שוב אין לו תקנה דאלמוהו רבנן תקנתייהו ואמרו כל שטר שנראה בב"ד דלא נעשה כתיקון חכמי' הרי הוא כחספא בעלמא:
שלא מדעת הלוה כשר שאין שם פסול עליו לאמר שאין בידו לעשות ממנו שטר בלא דעת הלוה ומה"ט נראה פשוט דס"ל דיכול המלוה למלאותו מדעתו בקרובים אפי' אחר היום שנחתם כל זמן שלא נראה בב"ד וכן מוכח באשר"י וכמ"ש בפרישה ע"ש ומ"ש המחבר בסמוך סט"ו דאם מלאוהו למחר כו' פסול לא כ"כ אלא לדעת הי"א שכ' בשמם בסוף סעיף זה דבעינן שימלאו מדעת הלוה וס"ל דשם פסול עליו כל זמן שלא מילאוהו וכל שמילאוהו שלא מדעת הלוה לא נשתעבד בו הלוה והוא דעת ר' יונה וכותיה פסק הרב המגיד משנה אבל הב"י דכתב עליו דעת הרב רבינו אשר שחולק עמו נראה עיקר וא"כ קשה דלא ה"ל להמחבר לסתום ולכתוב בסעיף ט"ו שלא כדעת הרא"ש ולכן נראה שהכל סעיף א' הוא והוא מצורף למ"ש לפניזה בשם הי"א ולהגי' וי"ו וצ"ל והא דמכשרינן כו' וק"ל:
meirat_einayim.en:
It can no longer be repaired. The Sages strengthened their enactment. Any document that comes before beit din and is found not to have been prepared according to their rules is treated as a mere shard and cannot later be repaired.
Without the borrower's knowledge, it is valid. No inherent invalidity exists merely because the lender has no authority to convert it into a document without the borrower's knowledge. For this reason it appears clear that the lender may fill the space with relatives on his own initiative even after the day of signing, so long as the document has not yet appeared before beit din. This is implied by the Rosh, as I explained in Perishah. The Mechaber's later statement in seif 15 that if they filled it the next day it is invalid was written only according to the 'some say' cited at the end of the present seif, who require the filling to be with the borrower's knowledge and who hold that the document remains in a state of invalidity until that is done. According to that view, if it is filled without the borrower's knowledge he was never bound by it. That is Rabbi Yonah's view, followed by Maggid Mishneh. Beit Yosef, however, writes that the Rosh's contrary view is primary. It is therefore difficult that the Mechaber later rules without qualification against the Rosh. It seems rather that all those words form one continuous clause connected to the preceding 'some say,' and the text should read, 'And the rule that we validate it...,' with a connecting vav.

siftei_kohen.he: שלא מדעת הלוה כשר. שאין שם פסול עליו לאמר שאין בידו לעשות ממנו שטר בלא דעת הלוה ומה"ט נרא' פשוט דיכול המלוה למלאותו בקרובי' אפילו אחר היום שנחת' וכן מוכח באשר"י וא"כ קשה על המחבר דלא ה"ל לסתום ולכתוב בסעיף ט"ו שלא כדעת הרא"ש ולכן נרא' שהכל סעיף אחד הוא והוא מצורף למ"ש לפני זה בשם הי"א ויש להגיה וי"ו וצ"ל והא דמכשרינן כו' עכ"ל סמ"ע ולא נהירא דא"כ לא ה"ל להמחבר לעשות מזה סעיף מיוחד אלא נרא' דס"ל דכ"ע מודו בזה דנהי דיכול לעשות שלא מדעת הלוה היינו כיון שמסר השטר לידו כאלו הרשהו לעשו' אבל מ"מ אין השטר נכשר אלא משעת המילוי וגם באשר"י לא מוכח מידי וי"ל דמודה בזה לה"ר יונה ע"ש:
siftei_kohen.en:
It is not a good idea. There is no need for him to say that he is not in his hands, and that he is not in his hands, and that he will not be able to do so, and that he will not be able to do so, and that he will be able to do so, and that he will not be able to do so
In this case, Dandi was reluctant to do so that he was not the science of the Levites, and that he had given him such a thing as he could do, but that he had no talent, but rather than the hour of filling, and that he was not too proven to him, and that he would not testify to him

turei_zahav.he: (בשם מהרש"ק בטור עד והם ממלאים אותה דבגיטין וכו') ר"ל לחד פירושא כמ"ש רש"י ועי' בטא"ה סי' ק"ל דפסק הטור דגם בגט פסול כה"ג:
turei_zahav.en: (On behalf of the PA in the column until they fill it with Dovgtin and so on) R. K.L., means that it is a “missive” and “in the beta” (C. C. K.C.)

urim_vetumim_tumim.he: דוקא שמלאהו ביום שנכתב וכו' ויש לדקדק על הש"ע דסתם הך דינא כאילו אין בו חולק ולענ"ד נראה לא סבירא ליה להרא"ש כן דהא רבינו יונה כתב הך דינא וכתב דאי ל"ת הכי אלא אפילו לאחר הזמן כשר משום דשטר כשר היא אלא שיש בו חשש זיוף וכיון שנסתלק הוכשר למפרע אם כן היכי משכחת לי' בהרחיק ב"ש דפסול כשיבוא לב"ד יאמרו לו לך ומלאו בקרובים ולהכשירו לשעבר. (ואין להקשות לפ"ז מה פריך הגמרא ב"ב דף קס"ב בין עדים לאשרתא דמטייט ליה א"ה בין כתב לעדים נמי דמה קושי' שם איירי דכבר עבר זמנו של שטר דבו ביום בלא"ה די ק רבינו יונה דלא שייך פסול דאפשר למלאות בקרובים ואם כן לאחר יום אף טיוטא לא מהני דה"ל מוקדם משא"כ בקיום לא שייך מוקדם ולכך מהני טיוטא וצ"ל דקושי' הגמ' אם כן דגם ברווח ב"ש מהני טיוטא למה קתני מלאהו בקרובים הל"ל מלאוהו בטיוטא כשר ול"ל קרובים ודוק ובפרט אם אמרינן דלכך קרוב ברישא כשר דהוצרך למלאו' החלל כי היה רווחא שביק למאן דקשיש וכאשר לא בא הוצרך לחתום פסול ואם כן קשי' שפיר עדיין יפסול דודאי לעדות נתכוון דאי למלוי הא יכול לטייט בדיו וא"ש) וי"א דאם בא לב"ד קודם שמלאהו שוב אין לו תקנ' ומילתא בלי טעמא הוא וכתב הרא"ש דהוא דבר שיש בו טעם לשבח ונתן טעם לסברא זו ע"ש ואם כן דסברא זו מסתבר כשל עוזר דכל ראי' ר"י לדינו הוא מהך דאל"כ הרחיק ב"ש דפסול איך משכחת לי' אבל לסברא זו שפיר משכחת בבא לב"ד קודם שמלאהו ולכך הטור ברמזים הך דינא דצריך המלוי להיות דוקא בו ביום השמיט והמתיק רק שיכול להיות בלי צווי הלוה וגם קודם שיבא לב"ד מהני מילוי ולא אח"כ והשמיט הך דינו דר"י והוא הטעם דלפי זה דצריך להיות קודם ביאה לב"ד אין לדין זה ראי' כלל ואם כן אף בטור יש לפרש כן דהעתיק דברי רבינו יונה ואח"כ הביא דעת אביו הרא"ש דסבירא ליה דצריך להיות דוקא שמלאהו קודם שבא לב"ד משמע הא זולתו כשר דדוחק דמיירי דבא לב"ד לגבות בו ביום שנכתב או דבאמת מחק זמן הנ"ל וכתב זמן ההוא שבא לב"ד וקיימו בש"א כנ"ל דמשמע דבא לב"ד בלי מילוי כלל אז ל"מ. וא"כ המחבר דפסק כרא"ש דצריך דוקא להתמלא קודם שבא לב"ד א"כ כשל עוזר ואין לדין זה של ר"י ראי' ולא ה"ל להביא בסתמא. והיה מקום לומר דסבירא ליה לרבינו מחבר מהכ"ת נימא דאם מילאו אחר כך בקרובים דיוכשר למפרע לגבות ממשעבדי במה חל שעבודו בהך שטרא הא תספא בעלמא הוא וא"א לגבות בו והוי כאילו לא נכתב כלל ואם כן מה צורך לר"י להביא ראיה בכך ודקארי ליה מה קארי לי' דכתב וכ"ת דמוכשר למפרע וכו' וצ"ל דודאי כל הפיסול דהרחקת שני שיטין הוא כשהעדים מוסרים השטר ליד המלוה ואז יכול לזייף. אבל כ"ז שהשטר תחת יד עדים אין עליו פיסול דהרי הם לא יזייפו וה"ל כמו גבי גט דכשר בע"מ ומכ"ש זה כשהשטר תחת יד עדים וא"כ אימתי מתחיל פסולו כשנמסר ליד המלוה ואם כן למ"ד עדים בחתומים זכין לו תיכף כשחתמו עדים חל שעבוד על נכסים דאז היה השטר תחת יד עדים ולא היה בו פיסול כלל רק אחר כך כשהגיע ליד המלוה אז ה"ל כנפסל ונמחק ואם כן פשיטא י"ל כשחזר ומלאוהו דחזר לכשרותו דהא שעבודו כבר חל מעת חתימה וכמו שטר שנמחק וחזר וקיימו ע"י עדים או העביר מחיקתו על ידי צפון ואם כן ר"י ורא"ש וטור כל ענין פלפולם הוא הכל למ"ד עבחז"ל דהכי סבירא ליה ולכך שפיר י"ל דלא הוי מוקדם אבל לפי דפסק הש"ע דלא כאביי רק בעינן דמטי לידו דאז חל שעבודו ובמטי לידו היה שטר שיכול לזייף והיה פסול לא חל שעבוד המלוה כלל כי האי שטרא הוי חספא בעלמא ואם כן במה יחול שעבודו ופשיטא דאם מלאוהו והכשירו לאחר זמן דלא חל שעבודו למפרע וה"ל מוקדם ואין צריך לראיה כלל ולכך סתם הש"ע דהוא פסול. ואיפכא לא קשיא דא"כ מנ"ל לש"ע הך דינא דרא"ש דצריך להיות קודם שנראה בב"ד דילמא אם בא בו ביום לב"ד גם כן כשר והא דקתני פסול בהרחיק ב"ש היינו בבא לב"ד למחר דשוב א"א למלאות דה"ל מוקדם ומנ"ל לחדש סברא ודין בלי ראיה. דהמחבר פסק ב' שיטין פסול לגמרי כדמשמע בגמרא וכמ"ש לעיל ס"ז ומוקדם סבירא ליה דאינו פסול רק למשעבדי ואם כן עדיין קשה איך קתני פסול לגמרי ימלאוהו בקרובים ויהיה מוקדם ולא יפסול רק למשעבדי ש"מ דסבירא ליה דא"א למלאות וא"ש. אך נראה דתלי' במחלוקת רש"י ותו' בגיטין דף פ"ב בגט קרח שקשריו מרובים מעדיו דג"כ פסול וא"כ לשיטת ר"י צריך להיות ביומו לתשלום הקשרים בעדים דכיון דהוא פסול מגזירה דרבנן ה"ל חספא ואיך יוכשר אחר כך למפרע בהשלמה ליום מחר דמ"ש דפסול מהך גזרה דיוכל לזייף או מהך גזרה דמשום כולכם סוף כל סוף פסול מגזרה דרבנן ואמרינן שם צא והשלים עליו עבד משוק ופי' התו' בד"ה צא כו' כי מילת והשלים משמע אחר כך שכבר נמסר הגט ורש"י כתב שעדיין לא נמסר הגט וכתבו התו' דנמס' הגט לאו דוקא רק שעדים לא חתמו ולענ"ד נר' נמסר דוקא דרש"י סבירא ליה כפי' ר"י דה"ל מוקדם ולכך פירש"י דעדיין לא נמסר ואם כן אף דנמסר ביום שלאחר כתיבה ל"ל בהו גבי גט דקלא אי' ליה בע"מ כמ"ש התו' דף י"ז ד"ה עד שעת נתינה כו' וא"ש ודוחק לומר צא והשלים היינו לאחר שכבר נגמר ומכל מקום הוי ביומו דזה דוחק וסתימת לשון הגמרא ודברי רש"י מדוקדק כמ"ש:
urim_vetumim_tumim.en: Specifically if he filled it on the day it was written, etc. Mechaber states this rule without qualification, as though no authority disputes it. In my view Rosh does not clearly agree. Rabbenu Yonah gives the rule and reasons as follows. If we were to say that even after the original date passes, a two-line gap can be cured by filling it with relatives, because the document was intrinsically valid and merely exposed to forgery, then the classic law that a two-line gap invalidates would become difficult to understand. Whenever such a document came before beit din, the court could simply instruct the holder to fill the gap with relatives and thereby restore it retroactively. Rabbenu Yonah therefore concludes that the filling must occur on the day of the document. If done later, retroactive validation would make the paper antedated. One should not object from Bava Batra 162b, where the Gemara asks why a two-line gap between the document and the court's certification cannot simply be smeared with ink. The cases differ. The Gemara's question is not necessarily whether later ink can retroactively cure a creditor lien. It asks why the Mishnah specifically teaches filling with relatives rather than simply saying the blank can be made unusable by ink. Particularly if relatives are used because sometimes valid people were initially expected to sign and later unavailable, one can understand why the baraita discusses that method. Rosh then cites another opinion: once the document has already been brought before beit din with the two-line gap, filling it afterward no longer helps. Rosh says this position has good reason and explains it favorably. If that is so, Rabbenu Yonah's proof for the same-day requirement is weakened. The classic case of a two-line gap can now be explained simply: the document is invalid when it reaches beit din before the gap is properly filled. There is no need to say that filling on a later calendar day is inherently ineffective. Indeed, in Rosh's abridged rulings the explicit same-day condition is omitted. Rosh says only that the gap can be filled without the debtor's authorization and that this works before the document is presented to beit din, but not afterward. This suggests that Rosh accepted the beit din cutoff and did not necessarily accept Rabbenu Yonah's additional calendar-day limitation. Tur can likewise be read this way. He first records Rabbenu Yonah, then cites Rosh's position requiring the filling before appearance in beit din. The plain implication is that Rosh's limitation replaces the need for Rabbenu Yonah's proof. It would be forced to establish Rosh's case only where the holder happened to appear in beit din on the same day as the document, or where he erased the old date and rewrote the date of appearance. Accordingly, Mechaber, who follows Rosh in requiring filling before the document is shown in beit din, should not have stated Rabbenu Yonah's same-day rule so categorically if its proof no longer remains decisive. There is, however, a conceptual basis for Mechaber's ruling. The two-line-gap defect arises principally when the witnesses deliver the document to the creditor. While the paper remains in the witnesses' own hands, there is little fear they will forge it. It resembles a get safeguarded by delivery witnesses, all the more so because the document itself remains under the witnesses' control. The defect begins when they hand it to the creditor in a form he can alter. According to the opinion that witness signatures acquire immediately for the creditor, the property lien can arise at the moment of signing, when the document is still safely in the witnesses' hands and not yet defective. Only afterward, upon delivery to the creditor, does the paper become exposed to forgery. In that model, later filling can be understood as restoring a document whose lien had already arisen validly at signing, much like a document that was later erased and then reconstructed by witnesses. It would not necessarily be antedated. This is the conceptual framework behind Rabbenu Yonah's discussion. But Mechaber does not follow Abaye's broad theory that the witness signatures alone immediately acquire for the creditor. According to Mechaber, the lien arises only when the document reaches the creditor. At that moment, if the paper still contains the two-line gap, it is a document capable of forgery and is legally defective. No creditor lien arises from a paper that is then mere parchment for collection purposes. If it is later filled and made valid, the lien can begin only from that later validation date. Using the earlier written date would indeed create an antedated lien. From this perspective, Mechaber's categorical same-day rule follows directly from his broader theory of when the document's lien begins. One may ask: then why does Mechaber also need Rosh's separate rule that filling after appearance in beit din does not help? Perhaps even on the original day, before the date becomes antedated, once the holder brings the defective paper to beit din the court has formally exposed its defect. The document is then judicially established as invalid in its present form. Allowing the holder to leave, fill the gap, and return would undermine the integrity of court procedure and invite manipulation. Thus there can be two separate cutoffs: calendar delay can create antedating because the lien did not arise earlier; presentation in beit din can independently freeze the document's defective status even within the same day. There is another proof for the same-day aspect from the laws of a bald folded get. A bald get, whose folds exceed its witnesses, is rabbinically invalid. According to Ri, the missing witness should be added the same day. Otherwise, if the paper becomes valid only on the next day, the earlier date can create the same retroactivity problem. The Gemara says, "Go and complete it with a slave from the marketplace." Tosafot understand the language "complete it" as implying supplementation afterward, perhaps even after the get had already been handed over in some sense. Rashi, however, explains that the get had not yet been delivered. In my view this disagreement parallels the present issue. Rashi is concerned that once the get has been delivered in its defective form, later completion cannot retroactively make the earlier date operative. Therefore he insists it had not yet been delivered. Tosafot read the case more flexibly and may hold the later completion can relate back under the particular get rules. Their phrase that "delivered" is not literal but merely means the signatures were not yet complete reflects this tension. It is difficult to say that the Gemara's phrase "go and complete it" necessarily means completion on the very same day. The wording is broad. But Rashi's explanation is exact if one accepts the concern that a rabbinically defective document cannot simply be repaired on a later day while preserving an earlier operative date. Accordingly, Mechaber's practical ruling can be defended even if Rabbenu Yonah's original proof is not decisive after Rosh's additional beit din rule. The better conceptual basis is Mechaber's rejection of Abaye's immediate signature-acquisition model. When the creditor first receives the paper, it must already be in a form capable of creating the lien. If the two-line gap remains, no lien begins. Later filling validates only prospectively. Therefore, to preserve the original written date without creating antedating, the correction must be completed that same day and before the defective paper is presented in beit din.

urim_vetumim_urim.he: אבל א"י לטעון להד"ם דהרי ניתן להכשיר במלאוהו בקרובים טור בשם רבי יונה וצ"ל דעדים עבידי למטעי ולהניח חלק ושבקי רווחא לשארי עדים דאל"כ הא עדים פסולים ופשיטא דיכול לטעון להד"ם ועיין תומים שאפילו ע"מ מעידים שכך היה השטר ברווח שני שיטין מכל מקום פסול דהוה שטר שיכול לזייף ובגט וכן שטרי קנין דדמי' לגט כמש"ל רמ"א ריש סימן מ"ב דעת הרמב"ם להכשיר בע"מ עיין א"ע סימן ק"ל ואם ע"מ מעידין על ש"א שכך היה בשטר מתחלה אי למדין מש"א עיין תומים דהוכחתי מדברי הר"ן דלמדין:
urim_vetumim_urim.en: But he cannot claim total denial. Since the deed could have been made valid by filling the blank with relatives, Tur in the name of Rabbi Yonah rules that the debtor cannot say, "Nothing ever occurred." We must therefore assume the witnesses erred by leaving space for additional signatories. Otherwise the witnesses themselves would have signed an invalid deed and total denial would obviously remain available. See Tumim: even if delivery witnesses testify that the deed originally had two blank lines, it remains invalid as a document capable of forgery. For a get, and similarly for acquisition deeds that resemble a get, Rama at the beginning of siman 42 cites Rambam as validating through delivery witnesses. See Even HaEzer 130. If delivery witnesses testify to what was originally written in the final line, see Tumim, where I prove from Ran that we may derive from it.

mechaber.he: הא דמכשרינן במילאוהו בקרובים או פסולים אם הוא שטר שאין בו קנין דוקא שמילאוהו ביום שנכתב ונחתם אבל אם מילאוהו למחר וליומא אחרא אפי' במצות הלוה פסול:
mechaber.en: The rule validating a document when the blank was filled with signatures of related or disqualified people applies, in a document without a formal act of acquisition, only if the space was filled on the day the document was written and signed. If it was filled the next day or later, it is invalid even if done at the borrower's instruction.

baer_hetev.he: שאין. ואפילו למ"ד עדיו בתחומין זכין לו. בשטר כזה דלא נחתם כראוי מוד' דאינן זוכין לו. סמ"ע:
baer_hetev.en: That there is not. Even according to the authority who holds that a document's witnesses acquire rights for the beneficiary from the time of signing, in a document of this kind, which was not properly signed, he agrees that they do not acquire rights for him. Sema.

beer_hagolah.he:
נ) ושם שם בשמו
ס) ה"ה שם דאילו יש בו קנין כבר נתבאר לעיל סי' ל"ט דיכול לכתוב אימת שירצה מזמן הקנין
ע) דה"ל מוקדם ופסול דהשתא משוי לי' שטרא

beur_hagra.he:
הא דמכשרינן. לדעת י"א הנ"ל:
(ליקוט) הא דאמרי' כו'. הוא לס' האחרונה דס"ל דהשטר חספא בעלמא אם לא כשמצוה הלוה ודוקא ביום וע' רא"ש שם אבל ס' הראשונה ס"ל דהשטר אין נפסל עד שיבא לב"ד דאלמוה רבנן לתקנתייהו כי היכי דלא לבא לידי זיוף אבל בלא"ה אין נפסל וע"ש (ע"כ):
beur_hagra.en:
That which we validate. This follows the latter opinion above.
(Anthology) That which we say, etc. According to the latter opinion, the document is merely a shard unless the debtor orders its completion, and then only on that day. See the Rosh there. The first opinion, however, holds that the document is not invalidated until it comes before beit din. The Sages strengthened their enactment so that it would not lead to forgery, but without that concern the document is not invalid. See there.

chelkat_mechokek.he: האידנא נהגו וכו'. הטעם משום דכולהו מסבלי והדר מקדשי והוא מנהג קבוע ביניהם והטוען תמורת המנהג אינו נאמן:
chelkat_mechokek.en: The ideo was used and so on. The taste of Hashem's wrath is a constant and he is not faithful:

meirat_einayim.he: אם הוא שטר שאין בו קנין כו' דאלו יש בו קנין כבר נתבאר בסי' ל"ט ובסי' מ"ג דיכול לכתוב אימת שירצה ומזמן הקנין אבל כשאין בו קנין אף למ"ד עדיו בחתומיו זכין לו בשטר כזה דלא נחתם כראוי מודה דאינן זוכין לו:
meirat_einayim.en: If he does not have a kimono in him, Kendall is already inscribed in the book to "T" and "Chappily" to write an impetus and the time of the canine, but when he does not buy any of his witnesses in such a string, he is not properly signed and admits to him:

netivot_hamishpat_hidushim.he: מלאוהו למחר אפי' למ"ד עדיו בחז"ל מ"מ כאן בשטר פסול לא שייך עבחז"ל וגם דעת הסמ"ע דלמ"ד דא"צ דעת הלוה אף למחר וליומא אוחר' כשר והש"ך כתב דבזה כ"ע מודים:
netivot_hamishpat_hidushim.en: They filled it in the next day. Even according to the view that a document's witnesses are treated as though their testimony was examined in beit din, that principle does not apply to an invalid document. The Sema holds that according to the opinion that the borrower's renewed consent is unnecessary, it is valid even if filled in the next day or on another day. The Shach writes that on this point everyone agrees.

siftei_kohen.he: אם הוא שטר שאין בו קנין כו'. ואפילו למ"ד (לעיל סי' ל"ט ס"ק מ') עדיו בחתומיו זכין לו בשטר כזה דלא נחתם כראוי מודה דאינן זוכין לו. סמ"ע וכ"כ הב"ח:
siftei_kohen.en: If it is a deed without a kinyan. Even according to the view that the witnesses acquire rights for the creditor through their signatures, that principle does not apply to a deed that was not properly signed. The Sema and Bach rule accordingly.

turei_zahav.he: (בב"י ד"ה וצריך שיקראוהו וכו') עד ולפי דבריו צ"ל וכו' ועי' ב"י בטא"ה סימן ק"ל שם האריך לבאר דברי הרא"ש אלו האיך תלוי זה בפי' הרי"ף ע"ש:
turei_zahav.en: (Beit Yosef, beginning “It must be read,” etc.) Through the words “According to his view it must be said,” etc. See also the Beit Yosef in Even HaEzer, siman 130, where he explains at length how these words of the Rosh depend on the Rif’s interpretation; see there.

urim_vetumim_urim.he: שכל המזייף כו' הן להוסיף בשיטה החלק או לחתוך השטר ולכתוב על ב' שיטות שטר חדש הכל אין הולך אצל הסופר לזייף רק מזייף בביתו ואי משערין בכתב אותן עדים החתומים על שטר זה או בכתב עדים דעלמא נסתפק בד"מ והרמב"ן הביא בחידושיו בשם ירושלמי ס"פ ג"פ דאם כתב יד הסופר גם משל עדים הולכין אחר כתב סופר ולעולם הולכין להקל סמ"ע וד"מ:
urim_vetumim_urim.en: Because anyone who forges, etc. Whether the fraud consists of adding text in the blank line or cutting away the original deed and writing a new one in the two blank lines, a forger does not normally go back to the original scribe. He forges privately. Darkei Moshe was uncertain whether the available space should be measured according to the handwriting of the witnesses actually signed on this deed or according to ordinary witnesses. Ramban cites the Jerusalem Talmud at the end of *Get Pashut* that if the scribe's handwriting is also present with the witnesses, we follow the scribe's handwriting. In general we measure leniently. Sema and Darkei Moshe.

mechaber.he: אם אחר שפרעו הוא טוען שהשטר היה פסול לפי שהרחיק הסופר חותם ידו יותר משטה אחת אין בדבריו כלום:
mechaber.en: If someone else is offended, he claims that the bill was wrong, as the writer distances his hand, there is nothing in his words:

beer_hagolah.he: פ) רשב"א מס"ס
beer_hagolah.en: P.S

beur_hagra.he: (ליקוט) אם אחר כו'. דהודאת בע"ד כמאה עדים דמי שהרי הודה בפריעתו (ע"כ):
beur_hagra.en: (Anthology) If afterward, etc. A party's admission is equivalent to one hundred witnesses, since he admitted that it was paid.

chelkat_mechokek.he: נידון כמחצה על מחצה. נראה דמיירי ששאר עיירות הסמוכות לה חלוקו' במנהגיה' וע"כ עיר חדשה נידון כמחצה ע"מ אבל עיר חדשה במלכות א"י או בשאר ארצות אשר אין חוששין לסבלונות למה תשתנה העיר החדשה מכלל המדינה:
chelkat_mechokek.en: He was condemned as a cross on the cross. It seems to me that the remaining towns that are adjacent to Koko in her custom and that a new city is condemned as crossing by, but a new city in the AJ or other countries that are not afraid of the sufferings of the new city of the state:

turei_zahav.he: (ע"ש ואינו פסול כו') עד דלכולהו אמוראי נמי וכו' לא דק דלאפוקי מר' אבהו כ"כ וכמש"ל בשם תיקון סופרים ק"ל ע"כ):
turei_zahav.en: (See there: It is not invalid, etc.) Through “according to all the Amoraim as well,” etc. This is imprecise, for it was written specifically to exclude Rabbi Abahu, as explained above in the name of Tikkun Soferim.

urim_vetumim_urim.he: כגון ל' בשיטה וכו' ואויר בין שני שיטות אבל אין צריך שיהיה הל' פוגש בקו של כ' פשוטה דא"כ צריך להיות חלל בין השיטות כשיעור ב' אוירי' זה לא אמרינן דיכול לכוון כתיבתו שלא יפגוש למ"ד בכ' פשוטה סמ"ע:
urim_vetumim_urim.en: Such as a method, etc. and air between two methods, but it is not necessary that the Almighty meets a simple line that must be a space between the methods as a lesson in 'Ori' that they do not say they are sufficient to target his writing that they will not meet the Almighty

mechaber.he: הבא מכח עכו"ם הרי הוא כמוהו לגבות בשטר שעידיו מרוחקים שני שיטים אם נהגו העכו"ם לגבות בו:
mechaber.en: One who derives title through a non-Jew has the same rights as the non-Jew. He may therefore collect with a document whose witnesses are separated from its text by two blank lines if non-Jewish practice permits collection with such a document.

baer_hetev.he: מכח. משמע דהמלו' הבא לגבות בא מכח עובד כוכבים ואף שהוא למעליותא ובסי' קנ"ד סי"ח פסק דדוקא לגריעותא הרי הוא כעובד כוכבים צ"ל דשאני הכא כיון דאפילו ישראל בישראל הי' יכול לגבות בו שהרי אנו רואין שאין בו זיוף אלא שפסלוהו משום שיכולין לזייפו ובשל עובד כוכבים לא התקינו להפקיע ממונו של זה הבא מכח עובד כוכבים משא"כ בסי' קנ"ד הוי איפכא דזה הי' מוחזק כמה שנים בחלונו וזה הבא מכח עובד כוכבים בא להזיקו בבנין שרוצ' לבנות ולהאפיל כנגדו וחילוק זה צריכין לחלק בסי' קנ"ד ג"כ דל"ת אהדדי מ"ש בסי"ח ובסי"ט ע"ש ומה"ט כתב המחבר בסי' ס"ו סכ"ה עובד כוכבים שמכר שט"ח לישראל כדיניהם דיינינן ליה שאם חזר ומחלו אינו מחול התם נמי כיון דקנ' ממנו השט"ח לאו כל כמיניה להזיקו בידים במחילתו גם מ"ש הרמ"א בסי' ס"ז סי"ז הבא מכח עובד כוכבים כו' ולכן מי שקנ' שט"ח מן העובד כוכבים על חבירו אין השביעית משמטתו דהתם נמי כיון דבלא"ה הי' זה חייב לשלם לעובד כוכבים ואין לו היזק בקניית ישראל חבירו נרא' דלכ"ע בכה"ג אמרינן דיש לו כח העובד כוכבים עכ"ל הסמ"ע:
baer_hetev.en: By virtue of. This implies that a creditor who comes to collect through a non-Jew acquires the non-Jew's legal position even where this benefits him. Yet in siman 154, seif 18, the ruling is that one who derives his claim from a non-Jew is treated like the non-Jew only to his disadvantage. One must distinguish: here, even between two Jews the creditor could have collected on the document, because we see that it contains no actual forgery; it was invalidated only because its form permits forgery. With regard to a non-Jew's document, the Sages did not enact a disqualification that would deprive the person who derives his right from that non-Jew of his money. In siman 154, however, the situation is the reverse: one party had possessed his window rights for many years, while the person deriving his right from a non-Jew seeks to harm him by constructing a building that blocks his light. This distinction must likewise be applied within siman 154 itself so that seif 18 and seif 19 do not contradict one another. For this reason the Mechaber writes in siman 66, seif 25, that if a non-Jew sells a promissory note to a Jew, we adjudicate according to their law so that if the seller later forgives the debt, it is not forgiven. There too, once the Jewish purchaser acquired the note from him, the seller has no power to cause him direct loss by forgiving it. Likewise, the Rama writes in siman 67, seif 17, regarding one who derives his claim from a non-Jew, that one who purchased from a non-Jew a promissory note against another Jew is not subject to cancellation by the Sabbatical year. There too, since the debtor would in any event have been obligated to pay the non-Jew and suffers no loss merely because his fellow Jew purchased the debt, it appears that all agree that in such a case the purchaser has the legal power that the non-Jew possessed. Sema.
